newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU differs over U.S. raid on Iraq - Spring.
newsitem.headline: EU differs over U.S. raid on Iraq - Spring.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring acknowledged on Thursday that there were "very different views" among European Union states about Washington's attacks on Iraq.

Spring, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency until the year's end, said EU reaction to U.S. raids on Iraqi targets would be discussed at an informal meeting of EU Foreign MInisters at Tralee, southern Ireland, over the weekend.

"Yes, there are very different views," Spring told Irish radio. "We will have an opportunity of discussing that at the weekend in Tralee, and I am looking forward to that discussion." He denied that EU states had "agreed to disagree" about the American policy.

The EU has yet to issue a formal statement on President Bill Clinton's decision to bomb Iraqi targets in retaliation for Iraqi incursions into Kurdish areas. Britain and Germany have strongly supported America's cruise missile strikes to punish the government of Saddam Hussein but France, Spain and Italy have withheld endorsement.
France's doubts have been seen as evidence of a weakening of the coalition which went to war with Saddam over his invasion of Kuwait in Operation Desert Storm in 1991.

U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher flew to Paris on Thursday to try to win French backing for the U.S. attacks over French objections that the Iraqi raids were not in breach of any United Nations resolution.

France has refrained from joining the United States and Britain in policing an enlarged no-fly zone over southern Iraq. France said on Thursday that the U.N. Security Council must reaffirm Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity in any resolution concerning Baghdad's offensive in the Kurdish area of northern Iraq.

Spring said EU member states had been in contact over the U.S. attacks informally and would have a chance to share their views during the weekend meeting. "We have had very informal contact over the past number of days. We have have an opportunity in Tralee to discuss matters at ministerial level."
It was the first time that Spring had publicly acknowledged that Iraq would be on the weekend agenda, which is expected to include topics ranging from former Yugoslavia to the bloodshed in Burundi.
Spring met Aldo Ajello, the EU's special envoy for Africa's Great Lakes region on Thursday and reaffirmed Dublin's support for a negotiated regional settlement.

"There is deep concern in Ireland and indeed throughout Europe that the situation must not be allowed to descend into all-out civil war. Already the scale of deaths has been horrendous," Spring said in a statement.
Carl Bildt, the international community's Bosnia moderator, will brief ministers on Saturday. Policy on other parts of the former Yugoslavia will also be discussed, Irish officials said.
Other items on the weekend agenda are expected to be the Middle East. Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy was due in Dublin on Thursday evening for talks with Spring.
